title: Proverbs 27: Boast Not of Tomorrow
body:
Read the chapter → [Proverbs 27](/bible/proverbs/27)

This chapter opens with the warning not to boast of tomorrow, since none of us know how much time we have, and moves through friendship, open rebuke, contentment, and diligence with what the Most High has given. The teacher ties it to James on the uncertainty of life, to the fixed line the Most High sets on a man's days, and to the crown that has not endured for Israel from one generation to the next.

**[Proverbs 27:1-2](/bible/proverbs/27#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/proverbs/27#v1)</sup> Boast not thyself of to morrow; for thou knowest not what a day may bring forth.
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/proverbs/27#v2)</sup> Let another man praise thee, and not thine own mouth; a stranger, and not thine own lips.

- Do not boast of tomorrow, for you do not know what a day may bring forth. James says the same: you do not know what will be tomorrow, for your life is a vapor; you ought to say, if the Most High wills, we will do this or that.
- None of us knows how much time we have. The Most High draws the line: Moses spoke unadvisedly at the waters of strife and was told he would not enter the promised land, and though he died in full strength at 120, the Most High set the end of his days.
- Let another man praise you, and not your own mouth; a stranger, and not your own lips. Do not be boastful.
  - **[James 4:13-15](/bible/james/4#v13)**
    > <sup>[13](/bible/james/4#v13)</sup> Go to now, ye that say, To day or to morrow we will go into such a city, and continue there a year, and buy and sell, and get gain:
    >
    > <sup>[14](/bible/james/4#v14)</sup> Whereas ye know not what shall be on the morrow. For what is your life? It is even a vapour, that appeareth for a little time, and then vanisheth away.
    >
    > <sup>[15](/bible/james/4#v15)</sup> For that ye ought to say, If the Lord will, we shall live, and do this, or that.

    You do not know what shall be tomorrow, for life is a vapor; you ought to say, if the Most High wills, we shall do this or that.

**[Proverbs 27:3-6](/bible/proverbs/27#v3)**

> <sup>[3](/bible/proverbs/27#v3)</sup> A stone is heavy, and the sand weighty; but a fool’s wrath is heavier than them both.
>
> <sup>[4](/bible/proverbs/27#v4)</sup> Wrath is cruel, and anger is outrageous; but who is able to stand before envy?
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/proverbs/27#v5)</sup> Open rebuke is better than secret love.
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/proverbs/27#v6)</sup> Faithful are the wounds of a friend; but the kisses of an enemy are deceitful.

- A stone is heavy and the sand weighty, but a fool's wrath is heavier than both. Wrath is cruel and anger outrageous, but who can stand before envy?
- Open rebuke is better than secret love. Many of us leaving the Christian church were shocked to see men stood up and rebuked openly, but the law does this so that people may learn to fear the Most High, as with Achan in [Joshua 7](/bible/joshua/7), who with his family and substance was stoned and burned before all.
- Faithful are the wounds of a friend, but the kisses of an enemy are deceitful.
  - **[Joshua 7](/bible/joshua/7)**  *1 But the children of Israel committed a trespass in the accursed thing: for Achan, the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took of the accursed thing: and the anger of the LORD was kindled against the children of Israel. 2 And Joshua sent men from Jericho to Ai, which is beside Beth-aven, on the east side of Beth-el, and spake unto them, saying, Go up and view the country. And the men went up and viewed Ai. 3 And they returned to Joshua, and said unto him, Let not all the people go up; but let about two or three thousand men go up and smite Ai; and make not all the people to labour thither; for they are but few. 4 So there went up thither of the people about three thousand men: and they fled before the men of Ai. 5 And the men of Ai smote of them about thirty and six men: for they chased them from before the gate even unto Shebarim, and smote them in the going down: wherefore the hearts of the people melted, and became as water. 6 And Joshua rent his clothes, and fell to the earth upon his face before the ark of the LORD until the eventide, he and the elders of Israel, and put dust upon their heads. 7 And Joshua said, Alas, O Lord GOD, wherefore hast thou at all brought this people over Jordan, to deliver us into the hand of the Amorites, to destroy us? would to God we had been content, and dwelt on the other side Jordan! 8 O Lord, what shall I say, when Israel turneth their backs before their enemies! 9 For the Canaanites and all the inhabitants of the land shall hear of it, and shall environ us round, and cut off our name from the earth: and what wilt thou do unto thy great name? 10 And the LORD said unto Joshua, Get thee up; wherefore liest thou thus upon thy face? 11 Israel hath sinned, and they have also transgressed my covenant which I commanded them: for they have even taken of the accursed thing, and have also stolen, and dissembled also, and they have put it even among their own stuff. 12 Therefore the children of Israel could not stand before their enemies, but turned their backs before their enemies, because they were accursed: neither will I be with you any more, except ye destroy the accursed from among you. 13 Up, sanctify the people, and say, Sanctify yourselves against to morrow: for thus saith the LORD God of Israel, There is an accursed thing in the midst of thee, O Israel: thou canst not stand before thine enemies, until ye take away the accursed thing from among you. 14 In the morning therefore ye shall be brought according to your tribes: and it shall be, that the tribe which the LORD taketh shall come according to the families thereof; and the family which the LORD shall take shall come by households; and the household which the LORD shall take shall come man by man. 15 And it shall be, that he that is taken with the accursed thing shall be burnt with fire, he and all that he hath: because he hath transgressed the covenant of the LORD, and because he hath wrought folly in Israel. 16 So Joshua rose up early in the morning, and brought Israel by their tribes; and the tribe of Judah was taken: 17 And he brought the family of Judah; and he took the family of the Zarhites: and he brought the family of the Zarhites man by man; and Zabdi was taken: 18 And he brought his household man by man; and Achan, the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, was taken. 19 And Joshua said unto Achan, My son, give, I pray thee, glory to the LORD God of Israel, and make confession unto him; and tell me now what thou hast done; hide it not from me. 20 And Achan answered Joshua, and said, Indeed I have sinned against the LORD God of Israel, and thus and thus have I done: 21 When I saw among the spoils a goodly Babylonish garment, and two hundred shekels of silver, and a wedge of gold of fifty shekels weight, then I coveted them, and took them; and, behold, they are hid in the earth in the midst of my tent, and the silver under it. 22 So Joshua sent messengers, and they ran unto the tent; and, behold, it was hid in his tent, and the silver under it. 23 And they took them out of the midst of the tent, and brought them unto Joshua, and unto all the children of Israel, and laid them out before the LORD. 24 And Joshua, and all Israel with him, took Achan the son of Zerah, and the silver, and the garment, and the wedge of gold, and his sons, and his daughters, and his oxen, and his asses, and his sheep, and his tent, and all that he had: and they brought them unto the valley of Achor. 25 And Joshua said, Why hast thou troubled us? the LORD shall trouble thee this day. And all Israel stoned him with stones, and burned them with fire, after they had stoned them with stones. 26 And they raised over him a great heap of stones unto this day. So the LORD turned from the fierceness of his anger. Wherefore the name of that place was called, The valley of Achor, unto this day.*  Achan, who hid the Babylonish garment, was stoned and burned with all he had before all Israel, that they might learn to fear the Most High.

**[Proverbs 27:7-10](/bible/proverbs/27#v7)**

> <sup>[7](/bible/proverbs/27#v7)</sup> The full soul loatheth an honeycomb; but to the hungry soul every bitter thing is sweet.
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/proverbs/27#v8)</sup> As a bird that wandereth from her nest, so is a man that wandereth from his place.
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/proverbs/27#v9)</sup> Ointment and perfume rejoice the heart: so doth the sweetness of a man’s friend by hearty counsel.
>
> <sup>[10](/bible/proverbs/27#v10)</sup> Thine own friend, and thy father’s friend, forsake not; neither go into thy brother’s house in the day of thy calamity: for better is a neighbour that is near than a brother far off.

- The full soul loathes the honeycomb, but to the hungry soul every bitter thing is sweet. As a bird that wanders from her nest, so is a man that wanders from his place.
- Ointment and perfume rejoice the heart, and so does the sweetness of a man's friend by hearty counsel.
- Do not forsake your own friend and your father's friend, nor go to your brother's house in the day of calamity, for better is a neighbor near than a brother far off. Jeroboam did the opposite, forsaking the wise counsel of the men who walked with his father.

**[Proverbs 27:11-12](/bible/proverbs/27#v11)**

> <sup>[11](/bible/proverbs/27#v11)</sup> My son, be wise, and make my heart glad, that I may answer him that reproacheth me.
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/proverbs/27#v12)</sup> A prudent man foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself; but the simple pass on, and are punished.

- Be wise, my son, and make my heart glad, that I may answer him that reproaches me. A prudent man foresees the evil and hides himself, but the simple pass on and are punished.
- Bishop has been preparing us with pantries and getting our bodies in shape for the next wave of the pandemic, which they keep tweaking and renaming as it changes strands; the prudent take heed while the simple pass on.

**[Proverbs 27:13-14](/bible/proverbs/27#v13)**

> <sup>[13](/bible/proverbs/27#v13)</sup> Take his garment that is surety for a stranger, and take a pledge of him for a strange woman.
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/proverbs/27#v14)</sup> He that blesseth his friend with a loud voice, rising early in the morning, it shall be counted a curse to him.

- Take the garment of him that is surety for a stranger, and take a pledge of him for a strange woman.
- He that blesses his friend with a loud voice, rising early in the morning, it shall be counted a curse to him. You may have worked fourteen or sixteen hours and are trying to get the last few winks before punching the clock, and a friend calling, texting, or banging on the door early breaks that sweet sleep. Ecclesiastes says the sleep of a laboring man is sweet.
  - **[Ecclesiastes 5:12](/bible/ecclesiastes/5#v12)**
    > <sup>[12](/bible/ecclesiastes/5#v12)</sup> The sleep of a labouring man is sweet, whether he eat little or much: but the abundance of the rich will not suffer him to sleep.

    The sleep of a laboring man is sweet, whether he eat little or much.

**[Proverbs 27:15-18](/bible/proverbs/27#v15)**

> <sup>[15](/bible/proverbs/27#v15)</sup> A continual dropping in a very rainy day and a contentious woman are alike.
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/proverbs/27#v16)</sup> Whosoever hideth her hideth the wind, and the ointment of his right hand, which bewrayeth itself.
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/proverbs/27#v17)</sup> Iron sharpeneth iron; so a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend.
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/proverbs/27#v18)</sup> Whoso keepeth the fig tree shall eat the fruit thereof: so he that waiteth on his master shall be honoured.

- A continual dropping in a very rainy day and a contentious woman are alike; whoever hides her hides the wind.
- Iron sharpens iron, so a man sharpens the countenance of his friend. Whoever keeps the fig tree shall eat its fruit, and he that waits on his master shall be honored.

**[Proverbs 27:19-22](/bible/proverbs/27#v19)**

> <sup>[19](/bible/proverbs/27#v19)</sup> As in water face answereth to face, so the heart of man to man.
>
> <sup>[20](/bible/proverbs/27#v20)</sup> Hell and destruction are never full; so the eyes of man are never satisfied.
>
> <sup>[21](/bible/proverbs/27#v21)</sup> As the fining pot for silver, and the furnace for gold; so is a man to his praise.
>
> <sup>[22](/bible/proverbs/27#v22)</sup> Though thou shouldest bray a fool in a mortar among wheat with a pestle, yet will not his foolishness depart from him.

- As in water face answers to face, so the heart of man to man. Hell and destruction are never full, and so the eyes of man are never satisfied, which goes into covetousness; we are meant to be satisfied with our own portion.
- As the fining pot for silver and the furnace for gold, so is a man to his praise. Though you bray a fool in a mortar with a pestle, his foolishness will not depart from him.
  - **[Ecclesiasticus 14:9](/bible/sirach/14#v9)**
    > <sup>[9](/bible/sirach/14#v9)</sup> A covetous man’s eye is not satisfied with his portion; and the iniquity of the wicked drieth up his soul.

    A covetous man's eye is never satisfied with his portion.

**[Proverbs 27:23-27](/bible/proverbs/27#v23)**

> <sup>[23](/bible/proverbs/27#v23)</sup> Be thou diligent to know the state of thy flocks, and look well to thy herds.
>
> <sup>[24](/bible/proverbs/27#v24)</sup> For riches are not for ever: and doth the crown endure to every generation?
>
> <sup>[25](/bible/proverbs/27#v25)</sup> The hay appeareth, and the tender grass sheweth itself, and herbs of the mountains are gathered.
>
> <sup>[26](/bible/proverbs/27#v26)</sup> The lambs are for thy clothing, and the goats are the price of the field.
>
> <sup>[27](/bible/proverbs/27#v27)</sup> And thou shalt have goats’ milk enough for thy food, for the food of thy household, and for the maintenance for thy maidens.

- Be diligent to know the state of your flocks and look well to your herds, for riches are not forever, nor does the crown endure to every generation. Israel is a homeborn slave; we held the crown only a short period and it has not endured from one generation to another.
- When the hay appears and the tender grass shows, the lambs are for clothing and the goats for the price of the field, with goats' milk enough for your food, your household, and the maintenance of your maidens.
